blocks.text: The chapter recounts Saul's defeat and death at Mount Gilboa at the hands of the Philistines. The Chronicler concludes by explicitly interpreting Saul's death as divine judgment: Saul died for his trespass because he failed to keep the LORD's word, consulted a medium instead of seeking the LORD, and did not inquire of the LORD directly. This theological interpretation grounds his downfall in spiritual unfaithfulness and frames the succession of David as God's righteous judgment.
